core_obligations: Identify a descent datum for the finite family with a descent datum for the single morphism obtained from the disjoint union of the members of the family, and check that effectivity is preserved by this identification (proof lines 1781-1786).
Reduce to the case of a single morphism between affine schemes (proof lines 1787-1788).

Identify descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves in that case with descent data for modules along the ring map on global sections, and note that this ring map is faithfully flat because the morphism is surjective and flat (proof lines 1788-1795).
Apply the module version of the statement to conclude effectivity, and note that the fully faithful part is the corresponding part of the same proposition (proof lines 1796-1797).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the family to the coproduct morphism (proof lines 1781-1786).
Reduce to one morphism of affine schemes (proof lines 1787-1788).
Translate to a faithfully flat ring map on global sections (proof lines 1788-1795).
difficulty_reason: For a standard fpqc covering of an affine scheme, the lemma asserts that every descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves is effective and that the functor from quasi-coherent modules on the base to descent data is fully faithful (statement lines 1766-1777). The proof is a genuine translation between two settings. It first identifies descent data for a finite family with descent data for the single morphism obtained from the disjoint union of the members of the family, and observes that effectivity matches under this identification, which reduces the statement to the case of a single morphism between affine schemes (proof lines 1781-1787). In that case descent data for quasi-coherent sheaves correspond to descent data for modules along the ring map on global sections, and since the morphism is surjective and flat this ring map is faithfully flat, so that the module version of the statement applies verbatim (proof lines 1788-1797). The claim is H2: two identifications have to be made and then recognised as preserving effectiveness, and the reduction to the affine single morphism case is what makes the cited module statement applicable, so the proof is a real derivation rather than a restatement.
